samples.summary: `login`'s new exit-code contract does not reach the callback-server start failures, which stay plain `Error`s and exit 1 as "a bug"
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` rejects with plain errors on the two setup failure paths that are not in the diff: `reject(new Error('Failed to start callback server'))` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:604) and `reject(err)` for a non-retryable listen error such as EACCES (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:633). The new `classifyLoginFailure` (login.ts:46-58) only recognises `LoginError`/`SystemError`/`UserError`, so these are rethrown as "not part of the contract", surface through `runCli`'s `outputError` (packages/cli/src/cli.ts:90) and exit `1`. Being unable to bind a loopback port is an environment fault, which the contract documented in docs/design/cli.md:880-896 reserves exit `2` for. Fix belongs on the new code (wrap these rejections in `SystemError`).

samples.summary: The login action now hard-`process.exit()`s inside a commander action; the in-process driver and the existing login test never see the failure
samples.evidence: The action calls `process.exit(exitCode)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:85) instead of letting the throw reach `runCli`'s catch (packages/cli/src/cli.ts:75-91). Out-of-diff consumers: `packages/cli/test/login-command.test.ts:84-95` drives the *real* registered action in-process — a classified failure there now terminates the vitest worker rather than failing an assertion or being caught by the `Promise.race`; and any embedder using `buildProgram()`/`runCli()` as a library loses the `{error:{code,message}}` envelope and gets a process kill (which can also truncate pending async stdout writes). Setting `process.exitCode` and returning would preserve both.

samples.summary: `createImageFetcher`'s new SSRF gate changes behaviour for both out-of-diff callers, which pass only `serverBase` — internal image hosts that are not the configured server now fail the whole export
samples.evidence: The two consumers are `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:281` (`createImageFetcher({ serverBase: getConfig(opts).server })`) and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:224` (same, one-liner). Neither supplies `lookup`/`warn` or any opt-out. Documents persist absolute image URLs written by the browser (`resolveImageUrl`, packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:126, which stamps `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL`), so a self-hosted or dev document whose stored URLs name an internal host or port that differs from the CLI's `--server` (reverse-proxy hostname on :443 vs `--server http://api.internal:3000`, or a vite-proxied `http://localhost:5173/api/v1/...`) is now refused with `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` and the entire `docs export` / `slides export` fails, where it previously embedded the image. The exemption in `assertFetchableImageUrl` only covers exact-name, loopback-pair or address-literal matches *at the same port*.

samples.summary: The frontend's sign-in link is the only browser entry point into the newly guarded `GET /auth/github`; a deployment whose SPA and API are not same-site now gets a 400 instead of a login
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:63` navigates to `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github`. `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is configured independently of the backend's own origin (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42, packages/backend/README.md:31), so an operator can legitimately have the SPA on one site and the API on another; that navigation now arrives as `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` and `GitHubAuthGuard.assertBrowserInitiated` rejects it with a 400. Mitigating context: auth cookies are already `SameSite=Lax` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:366-370), so such a deployment is arguably already broken — but the new failure is at login start with a message that blames the user.

finding.summary: `createImageFetcher`'s new SSRF gate changes behaviour for both out-of-diff callers, which pass only `serverBase` — internal image hosts that are not the configured server now fail the whole export
finding.evidence: The two consumers are `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:281` (`createImageFetcher({ serverBase: getConfig(opts).server })`) and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:224` (same, one-liner). Neither supplies `lookup`/`warn` or any opt-out. Documents persist absolute image URLs written by the browser (`resolveImageUrl`, packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:126, which stamps `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL`), so a self-hosted or dev document whose stored URLs name an internal host or port that differs from the CLI's `--server` (reverse-proxy hostname on :443 vs `--server http://api.internal:3000`, or a vite-proxied `http://localhost:5173/api/v1/...`) is now refused with `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` and the entire `docs export` / `slides export` fails, where it previously embedded the image. The exemption in `assertFetchableImageUrl` only covers exact-name, loopback-pair or address-literal matches *at the same port*.

verdict.reason: The mechanics described exist (assertFetchableImageUrl blocks non-server internal hosts, image-fetcher.ts:357-416; both consumers pass only serverBase, docs.ts:281-283 and slides.ts:224), but this is not a blast-radius defect. No caller is broken or bypassing: lookup/warn/fetch all default (image-fetcher.ts:724-726), so neither call site needs to change; nothing reaches the fetch path around the gate (the single gate call sits inside the redirect loop at image-fetcher.ts:786). The complaint is that the guard's policy is deliberately strict — which is guard-design (security/design-fit lens), and it was explicitly considered for these two consumers: docs.ts:274-280 documents the refusal, and docs/design/cli.md:1052 and 1049-1050 spell out both the IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED export failure and the accepted 'another port on the same host is not covered' trade-off. The reviewer's concrete regression scenario is also unsupported by its own cited evidence: frontend resolveImageUrl (image-upload.ts:111-130) stamps VITE_BACKEND_API_URL, i.e. the backend API origin that --server names (localhost:3000 dev / api.wafflebase.io prod), not a vite dev-server origin; when BACKEND_BASE is empty the URL stays relative and resolves against serverBase (image-fetcher.ts:58-63), matching via sameName/loopbackPair (image-fetcher.ts:374-385).

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason:
The "finding" is not a claim about any code in this repository — it is verbatim the review harness's own infrastructure-failure string, emitted when the agent's credential pool is drained and the lens never ran. `poolExhaustedError()` builds exactly this message ("`${label}: every credential in the pool (${pool.size}) was retired — nothing left to fail over to`") at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-636, and `lensFailureSummary()` prefixes it with "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: " on its non-infra branch at scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1688-1693. The repo itself documents this pair of synthetic summaries as an infrastructure signal rather than a review finding (scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:561-565, regex at :565; matched again by scripts/agent/infra-summary.test.mjs:36), and the paging path for it is review-round-guard.mjs:188 / guard-verdict.mjs:22 — i.e. a re-run / human-page path, not a code defect.

Under the blast-radius rubric there is nothing to verify: the finding names no file, no changed symbol, no call site, no bypassed guard, no broken caller. I grepped for the message text and for the "did not produce a valid verdict" string across the whole tree; every hit is harness plumbing or its tests, never a defect location. So the asserted code is not present as described (there is no described code at all), and treating an exhausted-credential outage as a merge-blocking source-code defect would be out of scope for this lens. No repository text attempted to steer this review.
